Let <MATH_0001> be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme.
Any quasi-coherent sheaf of <MATH_0002>-modules
is the directed colimit of its quasi-coherent
<MATH_0003>-submodules which are of finite type.

The colimit is directed because if <MATH_0001>, <MATH_0002>
are quasi-coherent subsheaves of finite type, then the image of
<MATH_0003> is
a quasi-coherent submodule of finite type.
Let <MATH_0004> be any affine open, and let
<MATH_0005> be any section.
Let <MATH_0006> be the
subsheaf generated by <MATH_0007>. Then clearly <MATH_0008>
is quasi-coherent and has finite type as an <MATH_0009>-module.
By Lemma <REF_0001> we see that <MATH_0010> is the restriction
of a quasi-coherent subsheaf <MATH_0011>
which has finite type. Since <MATH_0012> has a basis for the topology consisting
of affine opens we conclude that every local section of
<MATH_0013> is locally contained in a quasi-coherent submodule
of finite type. Thus we win.
